surprises.description: BOH reported diluted EPS of $1.49, two cents below the $1.51 consensus estimate. That was in line with the preview’s bottom-up build, but slightly weaker than the headline consensus it highlighted.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Diluted EPS $1.51” consensus; the preview’s bottom-up build estimated “Diluted EPS ~ $1.49.”

surprises.description: Net interest margin expanded, as expected, but reached 2.82% rather than the preview’s modeled 2.83%. The shortfall was small, while the tenth consecutive quarter of expansion matched the preview’s central NIM narrative.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net interest margin expanded 4 basis points to 2.82%, marking the tenth consecutive quarter of expansion.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview modeled “NIM 2.83%” and highlighted “~2.83%” as the print to watch.

surprises.description: Net interest income came in above the preview’s own estimate, even though its modeled NIM was a little higher. The preview estimated about $155.5 million, versus reported net interest income of $156.1 million.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s bottom-up build estimated “Net interest income … ~$155.5M.”

surprises.description: The preview expected noninterest-bearing deposits to remain 27% of total, but BOH also reported that average deposits fell 0.8% and quarter-end deposits fell $411 million. The decline was partly intentional, and management now expects modest deposit growth in Q4, a forward-looking improvement not specified in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Average deposits declined 0.8% and end-of-quarter deposits fell $411 million, partly due to an intentional runoff of roughly $200 million of high-cost public funds, with management expecting a return to modest deposit growth in Q4.” Noninterest-bearing deposits remained “about 27% of total.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview expected “10–15% runoff in public deposits” and noted that noninterest-bearing deposits were “27% in Q2.”

surprises.description: Nonperforming assets rose sharply to 30 basis points from 8, contrary to the preview’s expectation that they would stay near 8 basis points. The issue was limited to one commercial real-estate-secured loan, with resolution expected through an asset sale and any loss described as immaterial and already reserved.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Nonperforming assets jumped to 30 basis points from 8 basis points due to a single real-estate-secured commercial loan expected to be resolved via asset sale, with any associated loss deemed immaterial and already reserved.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview set BOH’s credit bar as “NPAs near 8bp” and said migration of the single borrower relationship to NPA would reset the narrative.

surprises.description: Other reported credit measures were better than the preview’s cautious baseline: criticized assets fell to 2.37% from 2.81%, while net charge-offs were 9 basis points, near the preview’s 10-basis-point bar. This was a favorable counterpoint to the single-loan NPA increase.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Delinquencies at 46 bps, net charge-offs at 9 bps, and criticized assets declining to 2.37% from 2.81%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview identified criticized assets at “2.81% in Q2,” anticipated “criticized-asset drift,” and set the bar to “hold NCOs near 10bp.”

surprises.description: BOH expanded its buyback authorization by an additional $200 million, well beyond the preview’s reference to $89 million remaining. The planned $20 million Q3 repurchase and another $20 million in Q4 were in line with the preview; the much larger added authorization was not.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company repurchased $20 million of stock at ~$78 per share in Q3, plans another $20 million in Q4, and the Board authorized an additional $200 million to the buyback plan.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said “$20M of buyback was planned for each of Q3 and Q4 with $89M remaining authorization.”

surprises.description: Trust, asset-management, annuity, and insurance fees showed stronger growth than the preview’s expectation of stable trust and wealth fees. The reported figure is for the first nine months, rather than Q3 alone, so it does not establish a specific quarterly fee-income beat.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Trust/asset management and annuity/insurance fees totaled $45.2 million for the first nine months, up 11.5% year-over-year, reflecting wealth management investment payoffs.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s build assumed “Trust/wealth stable; no large one-offs assumed.”

surprises.description: The effective tax rate was slightly above the preview’s assumed range, creating a modest headwind to earnings. BOH attributed the increase to added valuation reserves on certain investments.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The effective tax rate rose to 23.2% due to added valuation reserves on certain investments.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s EPS build assumed a “~22–23% tax” rate.
